summary: Jun Takashima specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1973 to ~1988 under Minoru Hara. He later held posts at Aichi Prefectural University, JSPS, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
Jun Yang is a scholar in linguistics, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, he held posts at Koyasan University and at the University of Chicago as Senior Lecturer in Chinese Language.

Jundo Nagashima works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Seitatsu Matsunami and Alexis Sanderson, earning his PhD at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams. He held posts at Taisho University, attested between 2006 and 2017.

June McDaniel is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She earned an MTS at Emory University and a PhD from the University of Chicago (1980–1986). In 1988, she was appointed Professor of Religious Studies at the College of Charleston.

Junglan Bang specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Seung-suk Jung and Sungdoo Ahn at Dongguk University and completed her PhD at the University of Hamburg in 2012 under Harunaga Isaacson, later serving as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and a PhD at Duke University under Stanley Abe, later becoming a professor at Keimyung University.

Junjirō Takakusu worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Oxford, Leipzig, and Tokyo under Max Müller, Sylvain Lévi, and Moriz Winternitz. His posts included Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, and President of Tokyo University.

Junkei Washio was a Buddhist studies and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Toyo University. He held professorships at Toyo University and Komazawa University, and also held a post at Sendan-Rin School.

Junkichi Imanishi specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ernst Waldschmidt. He served at Hokkaido University (~1969–1996), the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and as Chancellor of ICPBS (~1996–2020).

Junko Matsumura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She received an MA from the Australian National University in 1980 and a doctorate from the University of Göttingen in 1990. In 2011, she was attested as professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Junko Minamoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed graduate studies at Ryukoku University and Otani University. She has served as a commissioned researcher at Kansai University.

Junmai Zhang was a philosopher and Sinologist. He studied under Liang Qichao, as well as at Waseda University (~1906–1910) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1913–1915). He held posts at Peking University (~1918–1920) and Tsinghua University.

Junsho Kato specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at KU Leuven and earned a PhD from the University of Tokyo, studying under Akira Hirakawa, Étienne Lamotte, and Hajime Nakamura. He held posts at Nishogakusha, Nagoya, and Reitaku universities.

Juntarō Ishihama specialized in Iranian/Central Asian studies and Sinology. After studying at Kansai University from ~1906 to ~1908, he held academic posts at Kansai University (~1924–1961) and Ryukoku University (~1949–1965).
Junzo Inagaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoshin Fukihara and held a post as section chief at Otani University.
Juri Lotman was a linguistics and philosophy scholar who completed his education at Saint Petersburg State University between 1939 and 1961. He joined the faculty of the University of Tartu in 1954.

Jurij Andreevič Smirnov worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages (~1949–1954) and held a post as a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1967.

Shigeaki (Juro) Watanabe works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, and was a student of Gerhard Oberhammer. He held academic posts at the University of Tsukuba (attested 1989–1990) and as professor at Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003).
Jushu Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Bukkyo University as a part-time lecturer (attested 2005) and at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).
Justin Edwards Abbott was an Indology scholar who completed an A.B. at Dartmouth College (~1872–1876) and pursued studies at Union Theological Seminary (~1876–1879).
